entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Night by L Reziak with Swiss couple.  Mahomed showed us around.  Took us to his Fruit Garden.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove into Rezaiyeh, we stayed in the car nearly all the time, while Dad changed money etc.  Yesterday we had a blow out, so we had to go and have the tyre mended.  We met a student who spoke English, but unfortunately, he had a very bad stutter so it was difficult understanding him.  We went to see his ‘Garden’, it turned out to be a farm, 5000m2 big.  It grew apples, peaches, grapes, melons and a few vegetables.  We saw some sugar beet growing.  We bought two baskets of fruit, one of peaches, one of apples.  Then we took the mahomet back and drove to find our campsite by the lake.  We eventually found an official ‘Camping’ but everything was locked, and all the water had been turned off.  There was another van there, so we just drove onto the salt/sand and stayed there.  It stank because of all the salt, the lake was 25% salt.  There was lots of ‘sludge’ (green sludge) it was revolting, the other campers were very nice though.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Rezaiyeh and looked for a bank.  While Dad was looking, we got chatted up by some people from the Tourist Information and they helped Dad get some Third Party car insurance.  They they took us to the Tourist Information.  One of them had an awful stutter.  He was called Mahomete.  He took us to his farm.  It had apples, peaches, sunflowers and two donkeys.  The peaches and apples were The best I have ever had.  We bought 3 kilos of each.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We then went to the shores of Lake Rezaiyeh.  It was very salty.  There was another van there.  They had been driving for two years and gave us some delicious dates.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: There were lots of women in the streets wearing chouda which is a piece of big material like a shawl worn over all the clothes.  Someone called Mahomet helped us and took us to his garden where we bought a basket of peaches and one of apples.  The trees were watered by a stream.  F and I played in it.  The water was cool and very clear.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 32856 (5256 miles travelled).  Night in cornfield between Sonnate and Sanandaj.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We said goodbye to our friends and then drove off, through Rezaiyeh and on, down the road to Kermanshah.  All the women (well nearly all) wore a big chouda, which is a big thing of material, that they can wrap around them, completely covering them, except their feet, and they could pull it up to cover their faces.  It’s made of very light material, and they wear all their clothes underneath them.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We see lots of camels in the country.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Haman (pic).  We got IN and took our clothes off then we went into a room with a shower.  There was a bit down where we stood and an 18 inch bit round two edges.  We had a shower and soaped ourselves then we did our hair.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We had spent the night by a very salty lake.  It ponged.  F and I made a path of bricks and crazy paving in the water.  Dad walked on it without getting his thongs wet.  There were some Swiss and they gave us some dates.  They were on their way back from India and had a Siamese cat.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 33003 (5403 miles travelled).  Helped some Kurds.  Sanandaj Bazaar.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 33159 (5559 miles travelled).  Night at Taq e Boston

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stayed the night surrounded by corn stubble fields, some super flockes passed by, but they didn’t trouble us at all.  In the morning we drove on to Sanadaj, on the way we stopped and lent some kurdish people from a Landrover, our jack.  The women were wearing super costumes (not choudas) and Mum took a picture of them.  When we arrived at Sanadaj, we found the bazaar and walked round, it was very unimpressive.  There were lots of trinkets, but nothing old, or of good quality.  There were also lots of material shops, and people were buying new clothes or material to make into clothes, for the big feast on Saturday.  We looked for a ‘Hamman’ (bath-house) but without any success.  I read ‘The House of Elrig’ by Gavin Maxwell, it was an interesting book.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We were driving to Sanandaj, when some Kurds in a Landrover stopped us and asked for a jack.  The women all wore very pretty clothes.  Then we went to Sanandaj.  At the bazaar, I got a bulb for Dad.  It was 6 volt for the big torch, then we went to a bakery.  They got a bit of sticky dough and made a ball of it.  Then someone rolled it out flat and then someone else stuck it on the roof of an oil-lit oven.  One person got about 20 loaves, they were flat and oval.  We got 5 loaves, they were crispy.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to the country where the Kurds live.  The men wear quite baggy trousers and fringed turbans.  While the women wear very full skirts which were bright colours, some of them were embroidered with gold and silver thread.  Dad bought some very thin, hand-made bread.  While he got it, a nice girl came who could speak some English.  She gave us some pumpkin seeds to try, they were quite nice.  She was taking her washing to be washed in a big metal bowl, which she carried on her head.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Taq e Boston

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Night on road outside Hammandan, just past satellite station.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove through Kermanshah but couldn’t find anything.  We drove on and found ourselves in Taq-e Boston, where we finally found somewhere to camp for the night.  We drove back to Kermanshah, and drove round, we bought some biscuits and Francis bought an army hat.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Tickets for ‘Taq-e Boston’ (image), Coronation of ‘Ardeshir II’.  There were arches in the rock with pictures and carvings on them.  There were some super hunting scenes on them, with elephants.  We saw some ‘bas reliefs’, which were rock carvings in the face of some mountains very old, and the ones that weren’t very worn away, were fascinating.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We saw lots of ladies (and girls) with tin bowls full of washing up on their heads, there were lots of street sellers, some were frying fish in sweet smelling batter.  We bought some bread from a lady making it on the pavement over a fire.  End of Ramadam.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to some carvings.  There were two of hunting scenes and were very realistic.  There were elephants chasing wild boars and a man in a boat shooting them with arrows then some elephants carrying dead boars and on another wall there were people on horseback shooting stags.  They were being followed by elephants.  In one corner there were some camels in a train.  Also there was a much bigger horse with a knight in chainmail on.  It was very very realistic but bigger than lifesize and worn by weather and hands.  Also one leg was missing.  (pic - see 22 Sept - Taq-i-Boston ticket)

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: That night we camped at a park with no flowers, and lots of trees.  In the morning we went to some rock carvings.  There was a king on horseback, only half of him and his horse were carved out of the rock.  The horse had a lovely tail.  F bought an army cap which was green.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 33290 (5690 miles travelled).  Outside Hammadan.  Night 18km from Malayer.  Mohammed and Ali showed us round.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stayed the night just off the main road, going through some mountains, and in the morning drove off to Hamadan.  When we arrived, we found the bazaar and we went to a shop selling material for a ‘chouda’ for me, after a lot of sign language we eventually found some material that we liked and that there was enough of, the man explained that we needed 5 metres!  There were some ladies there and women customers, they and Mum draped it round me, so that we could see the general idea.  It was 450 rials (£3.60) for the 5m.  The pattern was just a little bigger than this and the blue was white, the white was blue, it was thin cotton, but not as thin and see-through as some of the other material.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We saw some dates, and bought a 6kg (approx) box of them, they were delicious, they hadn’t been pressed and were all soft and squidgy.  There were lots of copperware shops, with men hammering and melting, to make new things, and adjust old! Fodor (guidebook) said there were some nice leather coats, but we couldn’t find any.  On the way back to the van, we met two students who spoke English, and we asked them about leather coats, we pointed to a leather belt and one, (whose name we later discovered as Mohamet) said ‘O yes, you come, dis way’.  We ended up in a shop selling solely belts.  ‘Coats’ we explained ‘coooats’.  There was some whisperings in which I caught the word ‘corset’, which I took to be some Persian word.  We then set off again, Mohamet striding confidently along in front.  We ended up in a shop, with Mohamet pointing at a line of braces and yes-yes you want!  We think finally got him to understand when we pointed to some imitation leather coats, ‘Nothing like dis in my city’ he said, still we shall never know.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Hamadan.  At a bazaar the girls got some material for a chowdah (sic).  It was blue with white patterns on.  We also got six kilos of dates.  They were delicious.  Some people were making things out of copper.  They made huge plates.  I thought they would make super pizza plates.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to the bazaar in Hamadan.  Mum bought a big box of dates which contained 6kg.  We went to a sort of restaurant and had liver kebab and bread and peaches and apples and dates.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 33407 (5807 miles travelled)  Borejerd(?)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 33546 (5946 miles travelled)  Daram

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove all day.  We camped off the main road, in a desert of thistles, we drove Fred up an old river bank and just stayed there, there was a beautiful new moon.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camped at Hostel, Kasve Av.  No good.  Dirty and expensive.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We arrived in Isfahan.  We drove round in circles, following peoples instructions, until at last we stumbled on the main street, we drove up and down it for a while, following ‘tourist’ information signs, until a kindly policeman pointed a little side street out to us, we went up it (there were actually signs), and found the centre.  The lady there told us about two campings, and a place to eat out, the latter was invariably shut, we found another place, but the MCP (Male Chauvaunist Pig) running it wouldn’t let us girls in!  We finally found another place, and there, there was a separate room for women and their families.  Kebabs were v.good.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Went across a big bridge - it had lots of arches.  It was one way traffic.  It was very busy.  Dad found someone who worked in a Hotel.  He invited us to visit him tomorrow.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Visited Ali Qapu.  Royal Mosque.  Shah Abbas Hotel.  Shaking Minarets.  Bazaar.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Right rear tyre no longer mendable therefore abandoned.  Tube mended and new tyre put on.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Stayed the night in a campsite, nice pool, the rest not very good.  In the morning, we went to the ‘Kings Square’ we saw the ‘Ali Quapu’ and the ‘Masjid Shah’ (Shah Mosque) they were both very beautiful.  We went to see the ‘Shah Abbas’ Hotel (De-Luxe).  We had met someone last night, who was a bell-boy there, and he showed us round, it was very luxurious, and had some beautiful Persian art.  It was built on an old caravanserai, it was rooms built all round a big garden with a main bit at the front.  Then Moghers(?) showed us round the ‘Shaking Minaret’ and then we went to his house, and ate.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Ali Qabu - it was where the Shah used to get entertainment - and watched people playing polo.  It had tiles - not mosaics - because Shah Abbas the great was afraid that he might die before it was finished.  He did in fact die before it was finished.  The tiles were beautiful.  Some of them had gold on them.  Ones I liked most were of some animals and birds running wild.  There were lots of different animals.  I liked the snow cats best.  We took some photos then we went to the Royal Mosque.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to the Shah Abbas Hotel to meet the man we met yesterday.  He guided us to the shaking minarets.  We went in one, it shook a lot.  We found that when one shook, the other shook.  I bought a helmet.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to a place where the Shah entertained and watched people playing polo.  It was very high.  It had patterned tiles instead of mosaics because Shah Abbas the Great thought he would die before it was finished which he, in fact, did.  The thing I was glad about was that everything was so pretty.  There were some lovely shapes.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 33713 (6113 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We did some washing and things at the campsite and had a swim.  Then we went down to the river to have some lunch.  We walked along a super bridge, but some policemen told us to stop walking along the bottom set of arches, where the water came through.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: En route to Shiraz Mileage = 33844 (6244 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove all morning, but in the afternoon we went to visit some tombs, which were quite near Persepolis.  The first was by himself, it was the tomb of Cyrus I, and was near this royal palace, it used to have this inscription over the door “Oman, whoever you are and whenever you come, for I know that you will come - I am Cyrus, who gave the Persians their empire.  Do not grudge me this patch of earth that covers my body.”  Unfortunately it had been attached by cave robbers.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At [Naqsh-e-Rostam] there were four tombs carved into the rock face with some super bas reliefs carved on them.  They belongs to Darius I and II and Xerxes.  We eventually arrived at Persopolis.  Unfortunately, we could not visit the tent city, where the 2500 Persian Anniversary was held.  We visited Persopolis in the afternoon, it was magnificent.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Persopolis.  It was where Darius I and his tributary kings used to stay at summer.  There were lots of two-headed animals.  I liked the griffons best.  There were some gates with a King killing a griffin and a King killing a bull.  They were all bas reliefs.  There was also a parade of troops and chariots - all carved.  There were also some animals - some being carried, some walking.  They were very realistic.  There were gates about 60 feet high.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to Persopolis which is a summer palace and had some winged 2-headed griffins.  There were also horses and lions which were in worse condition than them and were super for climbing on.  It was when Denise and I got lost that we went to the Museum - it was a treasury but it had no silver or jewels but a little bit of gold.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we woke up, we saw some other cars, and a lady came up and gave us some breakfast, there were some vegetables and a bowl of meat.  The meat was all the things that we don’t usually eat, like tripe, there was also some tongue and it still had some hair on, dad buried it, but it was nice of them to give us some.  They came to talk, and in the end we were invited to stay at ‘Pariwashs’s’(?)  house, while we were in Shiraz.  We said thankyou, and then went off to see Persopolis, they gave us a melon and we ate it under some trees, where we met some students and shared the fruit. We sat talking for a long time, and then visited the ruins, and came back to have lunch with them.  We exchanged songs, and they danced a bit, they were fun.  At night we went to see the ‘son et lumiere’ at Persopolis and met a nice American man, who was travelling round on his own, he was very nice, the “Seth”(?) was very impressive.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We got up because some other people were making a noise.  When we had breakfast, they gave us some tripe and ox tongue.  They also gave us some lovely lemons.  We buried meat.  Then we walked about Persopolis.  Then Dad found some friends.  We had lunch with them.  They were very nice.  We took their photo and they took ours.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: When we had woken up and were having breakfast, a Persian lady came with some food which was meat with the walls of the stomach and some salad and some delicious but tiny lemons.  Dad found us some friends.  We had lunch with them and walked round Persepolis all day.  They sang and danced very well.  We buried half the meal.  In the evening, we went to a son et lumiere - it was Persepolis lit up and we got told bits about it.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 34012 (6412 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove into Shiraz and went to see Ali (one of the students) he showed us a tomb, it was like a mosque, it had mosaics of little ?? some were coloured.  Then we saw a palace, it was beautiful.  Then we went to Pariwash’s house.  We had an enormous Iranian lunch, it was delicious, they had a man servant, he was very sweet and old.  We went to see the tombs of Saadi and Hafez (both poets).  They were surrounded by beautiful gardens.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When we got to Shiraz, we found the lunch friends.  They took us to the lunch friends.  They had a boy and a girl.  The boy had a motor scooter and a train set.  On the board, he had a factory.  He took the furnace out and put solid alcohol in, then he lit it and put it in the factory.  The roof of the factory was like a boiler.  It worked a piston which worked a belt.  The belt worked an axle which turned two belts which turned a windmill and a kind of saw.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to a Mosque which had mirrors all along the walls.  It had an onyx floor and the mirrors were little mirrors put in patterns.  Francis found some pieces of glass - a piece was green and diamond shape and others.  We also went to a palace and gardens.  I wore my new skirt and things which I had bought in the bazaar.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went to the Bazaar with Pariwash, and bought Helena a costume, it was the kind that the Quash-Quai women wear, it was very see through and glittery.  In the afternoon, we went to see the girls, we picked Ali up, and then drove to the telephone factory to collect the girls.  We walked through gardens with them, and had our picture taken with them, and ate grilled corn with them.  We had Chelo(?)-Kebab for lunch.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Between Shiraz & Esfahan

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 34134 (6534 miles travelled).  In between Persopolis & Shiraz

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went to see some more tombs (3), with Pariwash.  The big gold and silver tombs, were each in a little mosque like building.  One had a museum which had a big old Clock and Bell from London on it.  It also had pottery, and many old ‘Korans’ (the Muslim Bible).  Mum, Pariwash and I had to wear chaudas, and everyone had to take off their shoes, as people prayed, and gave offerings there.  Then we went back and had lunch, packed and went.  We were sorry to go, and they wanted us to stay longer, but we had to go.  We had one last look at the bazaar and found a carrot juice place, we had some and it was very good.  Then we drove out of Shiraz dropped in at Persopolis, and then went on towards Isfahan.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the tomb of Shah Cheragh.  It had lots of small mirrors made into mosaics.  It looked beautiful with everything reflected a thousand times.  They were still making some of it.  I got some bits of mirror for H.  One was gold, one was red, one was green, one was blue, one was ordinary.  There was a museum nearby.  There was a suit of chainmail and a helmet - real old ones.  There were also some scimitars and shields also a big old clock.  There were lots of books, all very old.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: The costume I bought was a skirt, a top and two pieces of material - one red, one white - both with patterns of silver on them.  The skirt was red and black and blue and silver.  The blue and silver were streaked across the red, which is the main colour, with a black frilly line of material at the bottom.  The top is white with silver patterns.  The head things are worn with the silver and white one at the bottom as a veil for your hair.  The red one you tie around the top of your head.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 34279 (6679 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We camped just behind a little hillock, and just as I was about to go to the loo when a tractor drove up with a plough fixed on the back, he tried to say something, but without much success.  He gestured that we could stay where we were though.  All morning we were driving.  We had to stop for lunch, and rolled into Isfahan at about 5.00 o’clock.  We had dinner in a park and then drove round Isfahan in the dark, everything was lit up nicely though.  We looked at a few shops that were still open, and Helena bought a bangle for one ‘Toman’ which is 10 rials (8p).  We slept in a road next to the park, near the river.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We were driving to Shiraz when I saw some mounds of earth.  We stopped to explore them.  They had a mound of earth round a space - in the middle was a hole about 140 feet deep.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to a tower.  It was circular and made of mud bricks.  (pic) There had been a staircase but it had been washed away.  We climbed up to the top.  Dad took some photos.  On the way back, I found some blue wood like things.  They were nice.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Francis, Mummy, Daddy and I went to an old tower and climbed it.  I got stuck but, of course, Daddy got me down when we went we found some blue lice who lived in holes like ants nests. (Pic)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we woke up, we saw lots of boys going to school.  I wasn’t feeling very well so I didn’t have breakfast.  We drove to the ‘Friday Mosque’, it was surrounded by a small bazaar.  It was a courtyard with IWANS on all sides, and corridors with arches ran right the way round.  It had some beautiful tiles, but was unfortunately in very bad condition.  I was wearing my chouda, and a man asked F&H if I had changed my religion!  We had lunch by the river, and played a Turkish version of Bridge.  We had Chai there.  Then we went to see the ‘Palace of Forty Columns’.  It only had 20 columns, but by looking into the pool at the front, you saw 20 more reflected.  The others went to the bazaar but I was too tired and ill.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the Friday Mosque.  It was surrounded by bazaar.  (pic) In the bazaar we found the chap who sold us the helmet.  He told us that he and his brother owned two shops.  They chanted every now and then.  The mosque was made by lots of people.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to the Friday Mosque and on the way back we met our friend in his other shop.  (He owns two shops).  In that shop of general interest there were belts and neck-protectors.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 34447 (6847 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We slept by the park again.  We went to see the ‘Shah Loftalla Mosque’.  It was very beautiful.  Then we walked on to the Bazaar, F&H bought a shield and an axe, Mum & Dad paid for the shield.  I bought a hand-painted necklace, and Mum & Dad bought me some matching earrings.  In the afternoon, we went to a very good bookshop, we bought lots of books, we spent £10.  We got two Bible books and some books about Iran, we also got some fiction books.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the Shiek Lofteller Mosque.  The entrance was a small dark passage leading to a dome.  There were lots of paintings but not in bright colours.  Then we went to the bazaar.  Mum and Dad brought me and H a shield - a big one with knobs on it.  The handle was loose leather fixed in four places.  Helena and I brought an axe (pic).  It had two blades and a spike.  There were dents in the axe handle.  Denise got a necklace and some earrings.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to the bazaar at one shop (the only one I can remember) Denise bought a necklace of three crescents with silver things dangling from them.  I bought a mirror which looks like this. (Pic)

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to the Shahabas Hotel to see if mogaz was there.  He was not, so we went to lunch in a park and played(?) cards afterwards.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We slept in the park again, when I woke up, I felt a little better, so I had some cereals for breakfast.  After breakfast I didn’t feel so well again though.  A little girl watched us having breakfast, and while we were ‘doing things’ to the van she bought her little brother/sister, s/he was very sweet, I took a photo of them.  We went to see a nice garden it was surrounded by a beautiful mosque.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Helena and I started to colour her Paddington colouring book ‘A Home for Paddy’.  It was about Paddy getting found and adopted by The Browns.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Isfahan is full of lots of little bazaars.  I liked the brass best - especially the chainmail.  The shop I liked best was quite big and had three floors.  One room had a pile of helmets in a corner.  They had chainmail at the back.  In another room there was a pile of shields.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Isfahan Bazaar is really super, (I think), especially the brass section.  There is one shop that Francis and I like best and it has helmets, shields, axes and necklaces.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 34571 (6971 miles travelled).  Just out of Isfahan

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At 8.00pm we drove to the Shah Abbas Hotel, to pick up Mogados(?).  We drove to the bazaar, everyone except Francis bought shoes.  Mum and Dad bought a nice copper jug.  I bought a mirror with doors, it had a crack, so I got it very cheap.  I also bought a mascara brass jar.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: The mosques had lots of blue in.  I didn’t like them much.  I don’t know why.  Probably because they were too quiet for me.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: The moon rose very quickly because it was coming over the horizon.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I did not like any of the mosques.  In the evening, Francis and I climbed a mountain and found lots of walls and the place where a fire had been.  We carried over about ten big rocks.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I did not like any of the mosques but one room in the Shah’s entertaining house.  In the evening, F and I climbed a mountain and built a wall.  We saw the moon rising.  It rose very fast.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Campsite Tehran  Mileage = 34719 (7119 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove into Tehran and found the Poste Restante, Mum and Dad went in, we were waiting in the car, at last they came out, we were very excited.  I got two letters, one from Karen and one from Erica.  The rest of the day we drove round, the traffic was awful.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the crown jewels in Tehran.  There were lots emeralds.  The doors were one and a half feet thick.  I liked the holsters best.  Tehran is very chock-a-block and noisy.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Night outside Tehran

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We’re staying in a camping site just out of Tehran.  It’s quite nice, lots of lovely hot water.  Yesterday we saw the crown jewels.  I thought that the Empresses crown was nicest.  It was green velvet inside, and the crown had pearls, emeralds and rubies on it.  There was also the biggest pink diamond in the world there.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: There are lots of nice people at the campsite.  When we were washing clothes, Mum and I got talking to someone who used to know the Couchers(?), she used to go to school in Effingham.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had lunch in the campsite restaurant, they cooked hamburgers specially for us.  We left Tehran and found a little road off, there was a fox on the road and he ran in front of us on the road.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When we left Tehran, we were looking for a campsite, then Dad saw a road.  We went on a bit, there was a sign with a crown on! And a speed limit saying 40 miles an hour.  Then there was a bridge and a corner suddenly Dad saw a fox, we gave it a chase then it turned off the road.  We found a place to camp then we went exploring.  Helena and I found a big man-made rectangular pond with two pipes in making a waterfall.  The pipes let to a small ordinary pool with lots of frogs in.  It disappeared under a bush.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to see the crown jewels.  There were three crowns.  The one I like best had red velvet and the crown was silver and at the front there was an ?? ?? with a gold decoration.  I think Tehran is not very nice!  Too much traffic and not enough pizza but it’s quite nice.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Outside Tehran Mileage = 34811 (7211 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning we were driving through very barren mountains, we stopped at some holes and went to investigate, they were mine shafts, some went almost straight down, and had had cages going down and up them, we found one eventually that just went along horizontally, it was supported by wooden ‘pit props’ and water dripped through some of the roof.  We saw two big birds, Mum thought they were eagles.  When we were over the pass, and getting nearer the Caspian Sea, everything was suddenly very lush, with lots and lots of trees and other vegetation.  We drove out of the mountains, there were lots of newly harvested rice(?) fields.  We camped by the sea with some people we met at the camping site at Tehran, there was lots of lovely fine grey sand.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Helena and I went to explore the qanats.  They had been covered but the covers fell off.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we drove to the pass.  We saw lots of mines.  We decided to visit one.  It was a coal mine ?? the sides and roof to stop it falling in.  It was very dark and water dropped down on us.  There was a truck near one of them when we came out of the mountain pass.  It was really green because of the Caspian Sea.  We camped near the Caspian Sea with some people we camped with at Tehran.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We camped near Tehran by a leading off(?) road.  Francis and I discovered a pond with lots of frogs in it.  When driving, we chased a fox on the road then he ran off.  There was one adventurous frog and one frog who stayed in one place under our spot light (coming from the torch).  The frogs were a sandy colour with splodges of brown, green or greenish brown on them.  We went into a coal mine and saw all the pit props.  We have arrived at the Caspian Sea.  There is lots of greenery compared with the rest of Iran.  Some bits are like England.  F and I built a pyramid with a very small city.  There was one farm, a store house, a cafe and a place where the soldiers live in (a Barock ) and a huge pyramid.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At night we had a fire with our friends (Sharon, Dave, Kerry Little), they cooked some popcorn, we had it with sugar or salt, we all talked until it was quite late.  In the morning, we put on our bathing suits, it was very warm. We all swam in the sea (The Caspian is really an enormous lake, some 100 feet below sea level) it was all lovely sand in the sea, it got deep very slowly.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the afternoon, our friends went away.  Mum, Dad and I were having a siesta when we discovered that we couldn’t see F&H, I went to look for them, I went a long way and I saw a stream feeding into the sea, there was a water snake, it was grey with a black pattern on it.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We made a house in the sand (pic).  The walls were little lines to which we added small walls of sand.  We made holes for basins and baths.  When Dad came we dug a stream to an outside bath (which was H and I’s).  We swam a lot.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: H and I climbed a tower.  It was a water tower and all rusty.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We stayed at the Caspian Sea all day.  Denise, Francis and I (Kerry helpt a bit) built a house.  Francis and I made a bed and a private loo (made by digging so deep we came to water) - it did not get finished; we left it while swimming and someone spoiled it.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 34990 (7390 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 35139 (7539 miles travelled).  Dead badger.  Camped at Golestan Forest Park.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Two other vans came and parked by us, they were German, we made another fire, and talked with them, they had beer, but they gave me some Pepsi Cola.  (F&H were in bed.)  We woke up quite early, and were away before the Germans were awake.  We passed a dead badger by the side of the road.  We drove for a long time, we were hoping to reach the forest, to camp in, by nightfall, on the way we made a small detour to see a pencil-like monument.  It was someone’s tomb, and was over 900 years old.  We did in fact reach the forest and camped by the road, but when we were all in bed a warden came and told us (very nicely) to come somewhere else where it was better (he said).  There were lots of frogs.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We woke up earlier than the other vans and set off, without having breakfast!  On the way to buy some bread for breakfast, we found a dead badger, it was lying by the edge of the road.  Then we went to a tomb, it was in very good condition because it was built in 1006 and shaped like a pencil!

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to camp in the forest.  There were lots of roads but they all had barriers so we stopped at a barrier.  Soon a Jeep came and asked us very nicely to go to a better place.  So we got out of bed, put the roof down and followed him.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camped at Golestan Forest Park

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When F, H & I woke up, Mum and Dad weren’t in the van.  When they came back, they said that they had been looking for Ibex and had seen some, far away.  We all got dressed and had breakfast, and then F, H & I went exploring.  We found a big crab in a stream, we followed the path by the stream and came to a very very high waterfall (about 40/50 feet high, only a foot wide though) it made a pool, and the stream tumbled out of it.  We found some barbeque places and had lunch at one of them. While collecting firewood, I saw the carcass of a wild boar. We had fried banana, ham and jacket potatoes.  Later on, we were playing with crabs and Helena was holding one and saying ‘oh my little darling’ etc, when suddenly it pinched he and she really screamed, it was funny!  Later on we de-polluted another stream.  We also made a maggotery, we got them from bad acorns. [the maggots]

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We woke up at seven.  Mum and Dad weren’t there.  They had been looking for ibex.  They saw some but very far away.  H, D and I went to explore a path.  It led to a big waterfall.  I saw a big crab, it was about an inch long and much wider.  We took Mum and Dad there.  We found other ones, smaller than our one (smallest was purple and very vicious).  Helena was picking it up and saying ‘oh my darling’ etc when it pinched her.  She screamed.  (pic)

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Golegosten Park.  Francis, Dad, Denise, Mum and I had lunch.  Dad made a fire in a metal thing with holes in the bottom and sides and half of it was strips of metal forming a grill.  We fried four small bananas, eight slices of ham, roasted five potatoes (one small potato, four big ones) and three onions and two setts.  D, F and I made a maggotory.  We also found two red magpillers - a combination of maggot and caterpillars.  We found them all in bad acorns.  Before lunch we went to the stream.  Dad found lots of crabs - none as big as the one D, F and I found.  There was a little purple vicious one.  While I was darling it and shoving my finger in his face, he bit me and I screamed.  D, F and I went somewhere else and cleared a small stream from weed and polluted the clear water.  We did it just for fun.  We also cleared a pond with weed, fish and frogs in it.  We found a huge black crab, and a tiny one.  We went for a walk at night and saw one squeaky mouse in a tree.  They are dark creamish brown all over except their bellies, which are white.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Outside Mashad

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 35264 (7664 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We woke up very early (6.00), got dressed and set off, Ibex hunting.  We passed a dead fox on the road, it had been run over.  We scanned the mountains but couldn’t see a thing.  We drove on and made a detour to a little mosque, there was a pool in front of it, fed by mineral springs, there were lots and lots of carp (fish) in it.  Dad went swimming, he touched a fish.  He now has a cold.  Mum will show him no sympathy.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to a mosque.  It had a mineral water spring but was not hot.  They had made the water flow into a pool.  The pool was full of litter and huge carps.  Dad went and had a swim.  He touched a carp - 15 inches.  Before we went to bed we wrote lots of letters so that we could post them at Mashad.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have been to a carpfish pool, with carpfish in it.  They do not eat people.  The water is very clear and Dad swam but it made him ill.  We were not allowed to swim!!

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 35437 (7837 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove into Mashad, and just before we got lost, a man came up and asked us where we wanted to go, we said we wanted some gas.  After we had got the gas, he took us to the famous shrine where Iman Rezah was buried, we were only allowed to drive round it.  Just as we were leaving the shrine, Fred broke down.  We managed to get him going again, he stopped once more before we parked him.  Mohamet, that was the man’s name, took us to see an old caravanserai, we went right up to the top floor, there were lots of old carpets being mended, it looked very difficult.  Then we went into a carpet shop, and looked at some of the carpets and drank chai.  There were five which we really liked, so much so that we thought we might buy some, we went away to think about it.  We went to a public bath and then stayed the night outside their house.  We had some pomegranate juice, it was a little sharp.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Mashad.  A nice man met us, he had a Honda and took us to a carpet shop.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We have arrived in Mashad and gone to a carpet shop with our new friend.  It is on the top floor of an old caravanserai.  We were shown lots of carpets.  Out of them we loved 4 carpets - one had camel wool and sheep's wool.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning we went back to the carpet shop, and at last, bought 3 carpets, we bought a prayer rug, made with sheep and camel wool, a ‘flying carpet’ and a beautiful new carpet.  They were about £500 for all of them.  They were all made by nomad girls, and the dyes were all natural.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the Persian carpet shop.  It was in a caravanserai.  The carpets I liked best were a flying carpet and a praying carpet.  The prayer carpet had a bit for the body, you knelt there; two places to put your hands and a place to put your head; they had camel hair on, the rest was dyed wool (pic).  There was a man repairing a carpet.  He let me have a go but I did it wrong.  The carpet was on a loom.  The man was knotting, he used a hook knife thing to help.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went back to the carpet shop and had a bit of a gossip and Francis and I had about twelve lumps of sugar each.  Then, looking over the railing, we saw some wool which we went to feel, beside it was a sack of camel hair.  When we came back, we saw a man repairing a carpet on a loom, he knotted it, he tried to teach Francis, but he could not do it.  Then we went back and found Mum and Dad buying the carpets - the flying carpet, the new carpet, and the camel hair prayer carpet.  (Pic).

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We visited the Safarid Dam.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 35589 (7989 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Afghanistan - spent night at frontier.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove out of Mashad to an old Saffand dam, it was absolutely enormous.  We walked across it, and along the river to an old tower, it went down into the ground, as well as up.  It was very cold, and starting to rain, so we decided to ford the river, instead of going all the way back to the dam.  It was only 8 inches deep at the most.  We spent the night there and it rained and rained and rained.  We left in the morning, and drove to the Iranian border, it was quite foggy and rainy.  We saw a very funny group of camels.  We left Iran with very little trouble, went on 10km through no-man’s land to the Afghan border, they were much fussier and took a long time, so I cooked some tortellini, while Mum & Dad were away.  They took 2½ hours.  The bank has shut and we needed money for the tolls, before we got to Herat, so we spent the night near the customs.  We met a man who was bicycling to Australia and invited him to have coffee, we talked to him, he was very interesting.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: It had been raining all night.  When we got up, a cold wind made everything freezing outside, so we stayed inside but did not have breakfast because we hadn’t got any bread.  We saw lots of camels.  It got warmer til we were hot.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to the border. First of all we had to leave Iran. That took about 1½ hours. Then we went through the customs to enter Afghanistan. It took so long that we decided to camp at the customs.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to ye border and had to wait as least an hour and a half before getting out of Iran.  Then we drove ten kilometres to the Afghan border.  Mum and Dad came out after about 2 and a half hours.  We had to wait until we could have tortellini.  We could not change any money in the bank also - it was so late that we decided to camp there.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Later, a man came for coffee who hoped to bicycle to India.  He told us about his journey through North Africa and Europe.  Mum and Dad found him very interesting.
